126	What you want and what you think may be right, but
127	what you think, want and understand must be clarified: when
128	is the right time for it? If what you do is not at the right
129	time, you can miss out big. In truth, doing
130	something at the right time, one could say that this is
131	all of Judaism.
132	Judaism does not say
133	everything is forbidden. Judaism says everything has its place: a time
134	to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.
135	Everything has its own place. On Shabbat eve, lighting
136	candles is a great mitzvah; on Shabbat, the same act is
137	a great transgression. On Yom Kippur eve, eating is a great
138	mitzvah, a meal required by the Torah, a very important
139	and great mitzvah, to eat on the eve of Yom Kippur; and eating
140	on Yom Kippur itself is a great transgression. Do the
141	thing in the right place,
142	and you have gained enormously. You do it, you are in a rush
143	to do it, and it is not in the right place, you have lost
144	big.
